title: Take a different route home today and notice one new thing.
why: Small doses of novelty make days feel fuller and more memorable.
evidence: Heller et al. 2020 (novelty and positive affect)

title: Eat somewhere you've never eaten. Order something you've never tried.
why: New experiences are linked to brighter moods the same day.

title: Watch the sunset from somewhere high: a hill, a rooftop, a top-floor café.
why: Moments of awe shrink everyday worries and make people kinder.

title: Plan a no-phone half-day somewhere new within an hour of home.
why: Unplugged novelty is one of the fastest ways back to feeling present.

title: Get near open water: a lake, a river, the sea. Feet in if you can.
why: Time by water is consistently linked to calmer moods.

title: See live music by someone you've never heard of.
why: Shared live music builds a sense of connection, even among strangers.
evidence: Tarr et al. 2014 (music and social bonding)

title: Draw, paint or collage something for 20 minutes, badly on purpose.
why: Making art, at any skill level, lowers stress.

title: Sunrise mission: be outside when the sun comes up. Bring someone if you can.
why: Starting a day with awe changes how the rest of it feels.

title: Try a way of moving you've never done: a climbing wall, a dance video, a skate park.
why: Learning a new physical skill gives a quick, real hit of mastery.

title: Take a night walk somewhere safe and well lit. Find three stars or one constellation.
why: The night sky is everyday awe, free and always there.

title: Look up for one full minute: clouds, birds, the sky between buildings.
why: Even tiny moments of awe ease stress.

title: Day trip: pick a town on the map you've never visited and go.
why: Novel places are where memories get made.
